newsitem.title: JAPAN: More than 50 Japanese firms oppose MOF tax move.
newsitem.headline: More than 50 Japanese firms oppose MOF tax move.

text.p: More than 50 leading Japanese firms have issued a joint statement opposing a Ministry of Finance (MOF) plan to end exemptions on withholding tax on income gains from Euroyen bond investments, the group said on Friday.
An official of the Japan Securities Dealers' Association (JSDA) said the association was also planning to demand that the exemption be maintained.
The joint statement, from company executives from various industries, was delivered to the Finance and Trade Ministries on Thursday.

It was the result of a survey of 71 firms, of which 58 responded. Of the respondees, 54, including giants like Nippon Steel Corp, Toyota Motor, Tokyo Gas 9531 T, Hitachi Ltd and Tokyo Electric Power Co, said they opposed the MOF plan.

The statement called on the ministry to maintain the exemption on the grounds that Euroyen bonds were one of the most effective fund-raising tools and a much more efficient way to raise funds than domestic bonds.
It said the firms would face difficulties raising funds if the exemption was scrapped.
